newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spain Sept CPI moderates to 3.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spain Sept CPI moderates to 3.6 pct.

text.p: Spanish consumer inflation rose 0.2 percent month-in-month in September for a 3.6 percent rate year-on-year. In August, consumer prices rose 0.3 percent month-on-month or 3.7 percent year-on-year.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a monthly rise of 0.4 percent for 3.6 percent year-on-year.
Following are analysts views on the data:
ALFREDO URRUTIA, ECONOMIST AT SOCIETE GENERALE, MADRID
"0.3 to 0.35 had been forecast. If it was 0.2 we should have seen something lower in the year-on-year."
"Services continue their trend. Manufactured goods continue to perform very well"
"Inflation could reach 3.0 by quarter one 1997...We could be just about to break three percent at the end of the first quarter, yes".
"I wouldn't be expecting any real movement (from the Bank of Spain) in the next four to six weeks."
He said he doubted the Bank of Spain would be willing to cut rates beyond six pct before inflation hits three percent.
"It's starting to look pretty good for a further reduction in Spanish interest rates."
"I think we're likely to see the next move once the budget has passed through parliament. Maybe at the end of this month, 0.25 to 0.5."
"There's probably further progress to come (on inflation) and indeed further progress is required if Spain is to reach the Maastricht criteria on inflation."
"I think it's a distinct possibility that we might see Spain join in the first wave."
"The numbers are beginning to stack up, so it would be pretty difficult to exclude these (Club Med) countries".
"I think Spanish bonds will see a bit of profit-taking in the very short term"
